text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew says Singapore's General Elections results a sound and solid win for Peoples' Action Party and Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and his team.
- Lee says Goh and his two deputies had to act decisively in battle for Cheng San constituency, in which they attacked a Workers' Party candidate for "Chinese chauvinism".
- China warns United States of damage to bilateral ties by allowing Taiwan's Vice-President Lien Chan to make two U.S. stopovers.
- Singapore Airlines and India's Tata group venture of up to Singapore $100 million to set up domestic airline gets preliminary approval.
- Hutchison Paging and ST Messaging launch trial blitz to entice subscribers.
- Japan sounds warning on currencies and curbing U.S. dollars.
- Malaysian Ringgit rallies as international dealers move in.
- Tokyo stocks take a hard knock with plunge by nearly 3 percent.
- Toyota again overtakes Mercedes-Benz as Singapore's best-selling car brand in 1996.
- Electronics stocks make good start in 1998, with SES Electronics Index rising for sixth consecutive session.
- Chuan Soon Huat offers IPO shares at Singapore $0.35 each.
- India's civil aviation minister seeks to block Singapore Airlines and India's Tata group from setting up domestic airline.
- Securities Commission to release draft framework for 'over-the-counter' market on February 18 at seminar.
